$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Paysera Classifieds pilot loop graph.
Every day number, agent name, threshold and gate in README.md, INDEX.md,
the loop-*.yaml files, exit-conditions.json and pilot-brief-template.md is
derived from this file. `node tools/validate-graph.mjs` fails the build if
any document drifts from it.
TWO CLOCKS. The earlier version of this graph used a single 'DAY n' clock for
both the 30-day preparation window and the 30-day live pilot, which made
'DAY 30' mean two different things in two different documents. Days are now
explicitly namespaced:
P1..P30  = preparation window (this loop graph)
L1..L30  = live concierge pilot (starts the day after P30)
L31+     = post-pilot roadmap
v1.0 used the columns 'Kritinis | Būtina | Pageidautina'. Their meaning was
inverted between the count rows (critical = lowest bar) and the delay rows
(critical = latest date), so the same word meant 'floor' in one row and
'ceiling' in the next. Replaced by three unambiguous levels.
terminology.minimum: Below this the loop is FAILED. Not a soft target. Used only when direction = higher_better.
terminology.maximum: Above this the loop is FAILED. Used only when direction = lower_better.
terminology.target: The planned outcome. Loop is COMPLETE at this level.
terminology.stretch: Better than planned. Never a reason to extend the timeline.
direction: Every threshold declares its direction, because the v1.0 inversion came back.
with a prose note explaining that minimum meant ceiling in that one row —
which is the same word meaning floor in one row and ceiling in the next, i.e.
the defect this block says was removed. measurement_definitions carried the
higher_better  → minimum <= target <= stretch. The metric may not use `maximum`.
lower_better   → maximum >= target >= stretch. The metric may not use `minimum`.
Check S2 enforces this across plan.json thresholds, measurement_definitions

G1.name: lawful_basis_for_personal_data
$comment: REGULATED-ENTITY CONTROL. Paysera is a licensed EMI. No agent in this
graph may collect, query, enrich, store or contact a natural person -
customer or non-customer - before this gate is closed in writing by
Legal/DPO. In v1.0 Loop-D queried production transaction data and mailed
real customers from P3 while legal sign-off was only due on P14, and
INDEX.md stated 'Dependencies: None between loops'. That ordering is the
single most serious defect this revision fixes.
deliverables: Documented lawful basis per processing purpose (GDPR Art. 6), separately for: (a) internal transaction-data query, (b) profile enrichment, (c) marketing/recruitment outreach, (d) interview recording.
Written confirmation that AML/KYC identity data is NOT reused for recruitment (purpose limitation, GDPR Art. 5(1)(b) + AML law).
DPIA screening decision (required / not required) with rationale.
Retention period + deletion procedure for research data.
Approved outreach and consent wording (LT/EN), approved incentive amounts.
Approved list of external sources that may lawfully be scraped/contacted.
$blocks_agents_comment: Loop-E's three customer_personal agents were added on 2026-08-16. They were
missing because loop.gated_by was a single value and Loop-E declared G2, so
the graph asserted that building personas and a brief out of customer data
was authorised by a commercial scope sign-off rather than by a lawful basis.
G2 approves what the pilot may do. G1 is the only thing that authorises
touching a natural person's data, in Loop-E as anywhere else.
G1.on_miss: Loops A and D do not start. Loop-E and the CEO decision slip day-for-day. There is no 'proceed pending approval' path.

G2.name: pilot_scope_sign_off
G2.$comment: Signed pilot boundaries: transaction cap, prohibited items, verification level, dispute SLA, escalation routing. Loop-E may not synthesise a brief that presents unsigned constraints as approved.
deliverables: Named approver + timestamp from legal@paysera or compliance@paysera.
Explicit list of constraints that remain OPEN, to be carried into the brief as open risks.
G2.on_miss: The brief is presented to the CEO as 'scope pending legal sign-off' with the unsigned items listed on the first page. The pilot does not launch.

G3.name: publication_approval
G3.satisfied_by: CTO review AND Legal review of the drafted brief. Neither is an agent; both are named humans.
$comment: ADDED 2026-08-16. Before this, `legal_review` and `cto_review` were binary
requirements inside loop_e with due_day 26 — one day after loop_e closes on
P25. A requirement due after its owner has finished has no owner, and days
P26-P30 carried three milestones with no loop, no agent and no exit
conditions attached to them.
This gate exists because it is the repository's own founding rule:
generation and publication are two separate steps. The brief being drafted
is not the brief being approved. G3 is what separates them.
deliverables: CTO review recorded: technical feasibility of the pilot as scoped.
Legal review recorded: no untagged claims, no unapproved capability described as existing, G2 open items present on page 1.
Named reviewer + date for each. 'Reviewed' without a name is not a review.
G3.on_miss: The CEO presentation moves to a later date. A brief Legal has not reviewed is not presented. Being behind schedule buys a later date, never a skipped review.

data_classes.none: No personal data. Internal policy documents, own devices, synthetic or licensed sample data.
data_classes.public_personal: Personal data from public sources (marketplace seller handles, forum posts). Requires G1.
data_classes.customer_personal: Paysera customer data from production systems. Requires G1.
data_classes.customer_special: AML/KYC, identity-verification and payment-dispute records. Requires G1 AND an explicit purpose-limitation carve-out; default is NOT AVAILABLE for product research.

loop_a.name: Domain Expert Interviews
loop_a.goal: Understand the seller/buyer journey and its friction in real context.
loop_a.$depends_on_loops_comment: Empty is correct: Loop-A waits on gate G1, not on Loop-B finishing. A gate dependency is expressed by `gated_by`; `depends_on_loops` means 'that loop must be COMPLETE before this one starts'. Conflating the two would make Loop-A wait until P15.

interviews_completed.$source: Paysera-atsakymas.md: 'Pakalbinčiau 10–15 neseniai pardavusių ar pirkusių žmonių'. v1.0 said 15–20, which contradicted the letter it was supposed to implement.

theme_saturation.definition: No new themes appeared in the last 3 consecutive interviews.
theme_saturation.$comment: Tracked in exit-conditions.json since v2.0 but never defined here, so nothing constrained it. Not a count: it is a stopping condition on the interview series.

loop_b.name: Legal & Compliance Bounds
loop_b.goal: Establish the lawful basis for the research itself (G1), then the pilot's operating boundaries (G2).

binary_requirements.g2_signed_scope: MUST before pilot launch. May be 'open' at CEO presentation only if listed as an open item on page 1.

loop_c.name: Photo-to-Listing Workflow
loop_c.goal: Test the AI workflow from photo to structured listing and price range.
loop_c.$comment: Runs from P1 without a gate precisely because it uses no personal data: own devices, synthetic images, and licensed sample data only. Marketplace photos of real listings are personal data + third-party content and are excluded.

hallucination_rate_pct.definition: Share of generated listings containing a specification the device does not have, measured against the human ground truth recorded before the run.
$comment: PROMOTED HERE 2026-08-16. loop-c-photo-listing.yaml calls this the most
important safety indicator — a published listing asserting a spec the
device lacks is a misleading statement to a consumer on a regulated
platform. It existed only in exit-conditions.json: not in this file, not
in the YAML exit conditions, not a binary requirement, and absent from
every escalation rule, which escalated on quality score alone.
Loop-C could therefore complete at target with every listing carrying
invented specifications. A metric that cannot fail anything is a note.
It was also written `minimum 5 / target 0`, i.e. a 0% rate failed the
loop. It uses `maximum` now — see terminology.direction.

prompt_version_selected.definition: One prompt version is recommended, with the numbers and the sample-size caveat behind the recommendation.
prompt_version_selected.$comment: Present in the YAML exit conditions but in neither JSON file, which gave Loop-C three different metric sets across three documents.

loop_d.name: Repeat Seller Pattern & Recruitment
loop_d.goal: Identify and recruit the first concierge cohort from existing Paysera sellers.

cohort_profile_documented.definition: Cohort composition and categories documented, with the n=5 qualitative-sample caveat attached to every average.
cohort_profile_documented.$comment: Present in the YAML exit conditions but in neither JSON file.

loop_d.$incentive_comment: One incentive value for the whole cohort. v1.0 escalation doubled the incentive mid-recruitment (20→40, 25→50). Changing price mid-study biases the sample and treats late responders differently; any change now requires re-approval under G1. Escalate by adding channels and time, not money.

loop_e.name: Synthesis & Pilot Brief
loop_e.goal: Turn A+B+C+D outputs into one evidence-tagged pilot brief.
$gated_by_comment: G1 was added 2026-08-16. Loop-E declared G2 alone, and three of its four
agents carry data_class customer_personal. G2 is the pilot scope sign-off —
a commercial approval. It is not, and cannot be, the lawful basis for
processing a natural person's data. That is G1, in Loop-E exactly as in
Check C1 passed this because it asked only whether the loop named SOME gate
that closed before the agent started. Any gate satisfied it. Ordering was
safe in practice (G1 closes P6, Loop-E starts P21), so this was a modelling
defect rather than a live violation — but the graph is meant to be the
control, and it recorded no dependency on G1 at all.
$depends_on_loops_comment: ADDED 2026-08-16. Every depends_on in this file resolved inside its own
loop, and loop_e.synthesize_all_outputs — which consumes all four loops'
outputs — had depends_on: []. The graph had no edges between loops.
The real dependency lived in two unvalidated places: a depends_on array in
exit-conditions.json and a depends_on_completion comment in the YAML. The
ordering that makes this a graph was held by nothing except P21 being

untagged_claims.definition: Factual statements in the brief carrying no provenance tag. Zero is the only passing value.

tbd_count.definition: Count of [TBD] placeholders left in the brief.
tbd_count.$comment: Deliberately has no threshold. A [TBD] is an honest answer; an invented number is not. Tracked so the reader knows how much is unfilled, never used to fail the loop.

binary_requirements.provenance_complete: MUST. Every factual statement in the brief carries a provenance tag. An untagged claim blocks the brief.
binary_requirements.no_prewritten_conclusions: MUST. No synthesis prompt states a finding the agent is meant to derive.

$binary_requirements_comment: legal_review and cto_review moved to gate G3 on 2026-08-16. They were held
here with due_day 26, one day after this loop closes on P25 — a requirement
due after its owner has finished. See gates.G3.

milestones.label: GATE G1 — lawful basis decided in writing
GATE G2 — pilot scope signed; Loops B and C complete
GATE G3 — CTO + Legal review recorded; brief approved for presentation

$comment: ADDED 2026-08-16. G1's deliverables include a retention period and a deletion
procedure, and legal_basis_review outputs retention_days and deletion_owner.
No agent in any loop deleted anything, no milestone tracked it and no binary
requirement recorded it. The graph obtained permission to hold personal data
on a promise to delete it, and contained no node that kept the promise.
The period and the owner are [TBD] because G1 has not run. Putting a number
here would be inventing the answer to the question G1 exists to ask.
data_retention.deletion_due: [TBD — derived from prep_start_date + retention_days once both are known]
data_retention.binary_requirement: Deletion is executed on the due date and recorded with who did it and when. No substitute, no 'archived instead'.
data_retention.$covers_comment: Interview recordings are held in the tool G1 approves, not in graph/output/. They are covered by the same retention decision and deleted by the same owner.

$comment: v1.0 benchmarked a Lithuanian consumer-classifieds product against OLX, eBay
and Vinted, and sourced price comparables from an 'eBay/Vinted API'. The CEO
letter names the actual competitive set. Any competitor named in this repo
must appear in `primary` or be labelled with its `adjacent`/`excluded` reason.

primary_competitors.name: skelbiu.lt
primary_competitors.why: General classifieds incl. electronics — named in Task.md.

primary_competitors.name: autoplius.lt
primary_competitors.why: Auto vertical — named in Task.md; relevant for the L31+ auto expansion.

primary_competitors.name: Facebook Marketplace / LT buy-sell groups
primary_competitors.why: Where a large share of LT used-electronics trade actually happens.

adjacent_not_competitors.name: Vinted
adjacent_not_competitors.why: LT-founded, but a fashion-resale marketplace. Useful as a trust/logistics design reference, not as a used-electronics competitor or a price comparable.

excluded.name: OLX
excluded.why: Not a meaningful player in the LT market. Naming it as the incumbent signals the market was never checked.

excluded.name: eBay
excluded.why: Marginal in LT; its prices are not a valid comparable for LT used electronics.

price_comparable_sources.requires_legal_check: Whether automated collection from these sources is permitted is a G1 deliverable, not an assumption.

claim_policy.$comment: Prevents error category 1: invented facts inside a document that promised not to invent facts (Application-progress.md, 'Do not invent dates, metrics, team sizes, tools, ownership, or business outcomes').
claim_policy.rule: Every quantitative or factual claim in a published document carries exactly one provenance tag.

tags.[A:n]: From Loop-A, n interviews. n must match the actual transcript count.
tags.[B]: From Loop-B, with the source document or the named approver.
tags.[C]: From Loop-C measurement, with the sample size.
tags.[D]: From Loop-D data query, with the query date.
tags.[EXT:<url>]: External public source. URL must resolve and must be dated.
tags.[HYPOTHESIS]: Not yet evidence. Must be phrased as a hypothesis, never in the past tense.
tags.[TBD]: Deliberately unfilled placeholder in a template.

forbidden: Quotation marks around a sentence no interviewee said.
A template shipped with example results that read as findings.
Pre-written conclusions inside an agent prompt ('Išvada: …') that the agent is meant to derive.

sell_through_14d.definition: Share of activated listings that reach a confirmed completed transaction within 14 days.
sell_through_14d.$caveat: Baseline is each seller's own prior history, not a market average.

recommendation_score.definition: Mean of 'How likely are you to recommend this to another seller?' on a 0–10 scale.
recommendation_score.$comment: v1.0 called this 'NPS ≥ 7/10'. NPS is a −100..+100 promoter-minus-detractor figure, not an x/10 score, and it is statistically meaningless at n=5. Renamed and rescaled.

listing_time_minutes.definition: First photo upload to published listing.
listing_time_minutes.$comment: Was `minimum: 10, target: 5`, which read literally as 'a 5-minute listing fails the metric' — the v1.0 floor/ceiling inversion the terminology block says was removed, sitting in the source of truth. Uses `maximum` now.

ai_quality_score.definition: Human review of title + specs + clarity, 1–10, scored blind against ground truth.

pilot_constraints.$comment: v1.0 labelled a 1,500 EUR cap as 'the AML threshold'. It is not: it is a self-imposed pilot risk limit. Real regulatory thresholds are a Loop-B deliverable, not something this document may assert.

escrow_hold_days.$comment: Protected payment for consumer classifieds is a hypothesis pending legal/compliance validation (Paysera-atsakymas.md). It must never be described as an existing Paysera feature.
